name: NC-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 23 points
Incumbent Valerie Foushee running for reelection with large financial advantage
Republican challenger raised only about $12,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price Foushee at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Foushee: a 23-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a massive fundraising edge over a challenger who has raised barely $12,000. Prediction markets agree, pricing her win probability near 96%, so the only real question is the size of her margin.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending against Foushee or an unexpected polling error in North Carolina's Research Triangle area could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Valerie Foushee, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking reelection in a North Carolina district that leans about 23 points Democratic. She has raised more than $900,000 and benefits from roughly $2.4 million in outside support, while her Republican challenger, Max Ganorkar, has raised under $12,000 and drawn no outside help. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but has no visible campaign resources.

No public general-election polls cover this race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which give Foushee about a 96 percent chance of winning. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being whether the margin lands closer to 20 points or well above 30.
